result.reasoning:
The mechanism is real (steer.py:432 makes the blend NaN wherever the candidate is NaN, while ctx._pool_rows at steer.py:443-446 is built once on pu's full universe), but on the inputs this batch actually fed it the term is either identically zero or inside the project's own ±0.3 noise band, and it cannot change any number or conclusion that is reported.

(1) UNREACHABLE FOR THE CANDIDATES THAT MATTER. The pool is `cs_last_high20(neg(cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30)), cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15))` (guidance/B01.yaml:134). In AlphaCube `cross_mean`/`cross_max` are `rolling_reduce(nanmean_last / nanmax_last)` over NaN-LEFT-PADDED windows (src/alphacube/operators/common.py:426-453, dt_cross.py:223-237): finite iff the input is finite on >=1 of the last d days. `cross_ema` (partura/ops_ext.py:170-200) is finite from a name's FIRST finite day on and its denominator decays at only 0.9971/day at d=241. Idea I2's whole memory vocabulary is `{cross_ema, cross_mean}` with windows {10,30,60}, so a memory-rooted candidate's finite set is a SUPERSET of the pool's and `isfinite(z) & isfinite(pu) == isfinite(pu)` — the blend lives in exactly the pool's universe and the universe term is 0, not small. Measured with the real operators on a ragged panel (listings staggered + suspension runs): pool-finite cells missed = 0 for cross_ema at d=10/30/60/241 and for cross_mean at d>=30; only `cross_mean(.,10)` (1.4%) and a bare day-op root with no memory op (7.0%) miss any. In episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json the eight candidates nearest THR are ALL `cross_ema(...,241)`-rooted over `day_gini(Low)` (`abs_` preserves NaN), i.e. exactly zero bias; the bare-day-op-rooted ones (`day_es_ratio_hi(High)`, `abs_(cs_demean(day_gini(Low)))`, `day_sum(nt_ts_var(Amt,3))`) sit at -0.94..-2.91, 1.1-3.1 BELOW the 0.2 threshold.

(2) THE QUOTED MAGNITUDES DO NOT TRANSFER. tmp/review/reward-math/t2d_coverage_sweep.py reproduces as reported (-0.274/-0.484/-0.972/-1.763), but that world has S=400 names, an injected persistent cross-sectional mean-return gradient `extra = np.linspace(0, 0.0008, S)` (= 20%/yr spread) and the missing names sorted on REALISED return. Rebuilt on the actual grid (1359 days, ~3600 labelled names/day per notes/F101, pool pure-long book calibrated to the repo's own +11..+17%/yr at Sharpe +1.9..+3.1, vol 5.8%/yr per handoff/F111.../work_R1_*.md), the same "pool copy with missing names, true marginal 0" gives: 10% of names at random -0.127 ± 0.079 (8 draws, worst -0.246); 10% = the pool's own favourite names -0.04..-0.18; 10% sorted on realised return -0.73 (and that in-sample sort is not available to a data-driven NaN mask); random missing CELLS is the only pattern that passes 0.3, and it is purely the 15 bp cost of the churn the blend's own NaNs create — -0.163 per 1% of flickering cells after rescaling to the real book vol, with a matching +0.97 pp of blend one-sided turnover per 1% flicker. The e1 blend turnovers on disk are 2.51-13.88% (median 4.12%) and 3.06-3.85% for the near-threshold candidates, i.e. no flicker signature there.

(3) IT CANNOT MANUFACTURE A DISCOVERY. The flicker channel is strictly negative (a cost). The persistent channel's positive side is killed by R4's `score = min(score_train, score_valid)`: dropping the HIGHEST-realised-return 5%/10% of names still scores -0.186/-0.116, and the best of 40 random 10% name drops is +0.030 (+0.020 rescaled) against THR = 0.2. So the term can only depress already-failing candidates, never create a passer.

(4) NOTHING REPORTED DEPENDS ON IT. The only long_marginal artefact on disk is episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json, and handoff/COORDINATOR.md already retracts it, for this exact class of reason: "e1(首跑)的结论作废:对池子的边际奖励两边股票池不一致(已修:RewardContext.pool_in_universe)". The e2 rerun (192/arm) is in flight. The "same range and sign this bug produces" argument also fails: solving `score = min(train - Bt, valid - Bv)` on all 160 archive rows gives ONE common pool-alone Sharpe, train 2.7846 / valid 4.1030, reproducing every score to 1e-6, with valid the binding leg for 152 of 160 rows. The uniform negativity is just a 50/50 dilution of a Sharpe-2.78/4.10 book — no universe term needed, and no candidate was within 0.82 of THR.

RESIDUAL (why this is not a nothing): for a FUTURE bare-day-op-rooted candidate (no memory op at the root, ~7% of pool-finite cells missed in the ragged test, i.e. suspension-resumption days) the depression is up to ~-0.5, which is outside the ±0.3 band. That is a false-negative risk for e2, not a wrong reported number, and it is worth fixing; the reporter's own suggested fix is the wrong one (see corrected_fix).

result.corrected_fix:
The defect is not worth a code change for e1/e2's reported numbers, but if it is fixed anyway, do NOT use the suggested line. `sm = np.where(np.isfinite(pu), np.where(np.isfinite(z), 0.5*z + 0.5*pu, pu), np.nan)` introduces a new scale bug: for covered names the score is `0.5*z + 0.5*pu` (sd ≈ 0.71 × sd(pu) when z and pu are near-independent), while uncovered names get bare `pu` (sd = sd(pu)). The uncovered names therefore occupy both tails disproportionately and crowd into the top decile — so a candidate's coverage would still move its own book, just through the other end of the mechanism, and the effect again grows with missing coverage.

Correct option A (preferred, and the only one that literally honours pool_in_universe's own docstring): keep the blend on the candidate's universe and restrict the pool to the same cells, keying the cache on the coverage mask instead of dropping it:

    key = hash(np.isfinite(sm).tobytes())            # or the packed mask
    if ctx._pool_rows is None or ctx._pool_rows[0] != key:
        pm = np.where(np.isfinite(sm), ctx.pool_in_universe(), np.nan)
        ctx._pool_rows = (key, bk.book_row(pm, ctx.tgt, ctx.train), bk.book_row(pm, ctx.tgt, ctx.valid))

The reporter's cost objection does not hold: the mask is identical for every full-coverage candidate and for all 56 cross_ema-rooted ones, so the cache still hits on the large majority; and `reward()` already runs 4 train book_rows + 1 valid book_row per candidate (halflives (0.0, 5, 20) x 2 signs in idea_search.py:103), against ~4.1 s of total scoring time per candidate (evidence.json: scoring_seconds 503 / scored 123), so two extra book_rows on a cache miss is roughly +20-40% of reward(), not a doubling.

Correct option B (cheap, keeps the single cached pool row): fill on the pool's universe and then RE-RANK, so both groups share one scale — `fill = np.where(np.isfinite(pu), np.where(np.isfinite(z), 0.5*z + 0.5*pu, pu), np.nan); sm = dg._zrank(fill)`. Re-ranking is what removes the variance mismatch; the suggested fix without it is wrong.

Either way, also tighten the gate so this stays unreachable: the coverage gate in idea_search.py:129 is measured against the label grid (`min_coverage=0.9` of labelled cells), not against the pool, so a candidate may be NaN on up to 10% of the cells the pool trades. Gate on `isfinite(panel) | ~isfinite(pool_in_universe())` instead, and record the realised candidate-vs-pool coverage in evidence.json so the term is auditable after the fact rather than re-derived from synthetic worlds.
